messages:
carla: Quick prototype pitch — I'm trying a small router-side proxy that does lightweight prefetch/KV warmup + candidate scoring before calling the main policy engine. Goal: shave ms off cold-paths without touching policy runtime. wanna sanity-check interface tradeoffs.
ben: sounds interesting. main concerns: duplication of logic, consistency with policy decisions, and how we surface telemetry.
carla: yep. design idea: proxy accepts a minimal request envelope, runs fast heuristics (geo, last-successful-route, cached KV hints), issues a tiny prefetch to the runtime (non-blocking) and returns an enriched request to the policy engine.
alice: how do you avoid divergence where proxy picks a candidate and policy engine later chooses a different one? That could hide regressions.
carla: good point. plan is proxy never makes final routing decisions — only annotates the request with ordered hints + confidence scores. policy engine remains authority. proxy hints are only advisory.
omar (pm): from SLA POV: will hints ever be used as tie-breakers if policy engine is overloaded? need to know fallback semantics for product.
carla: two modes: strict (engine ignores hints except for telemetry) and assist (engine can use hints to bias selection under timeouts). controlled by tenant config.
ben: assist mode sounds useful but risky. we need a clear staleness TTL on hints and strong provenance tagging so we can reason about regressions.
ria: +1 for provenance. also: telemetry must show when hint-influenced routes were picked and the resulting latencies/costs. otherwise ops can't debug.
dave: perf question: proxy prefetch could add extra load on runtime (double work). have you measured net gain vs wasted prefetches?
carla: rough sim: for tail-cold paths (<5% of requests) prefetch saves ~30-50ms per request with 10-15% extra token work. for hot paths payback is negative, so proxy will sample & backoff dynamically.
ben: ok sampling/backoff critical. also need backpressure signals so proxy can stop prefetching when runtime is saturated.
carla: yep plan is to subscribe to a small runtime health topic (latency/cpu pressure) via our existing pubsub. infra-bot will broadcast.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary 1/3 proxy: succeeded — cpu impact +3%, p50 ~ +1ms, cold-p90 down ~40ms.
alice: that infra-bot report is encouraging. but still want a litmus test for correctness: if proxy hints hide a model-compat problem, we need a forced path to bypass hints for canary traffic.
carla: agreed. we'll add a header x-router-proxy-bypass=true for canaries and internal eval traffic.
omar (pm): product ask: expose toggle per-tenant in Console? ops should be able to flip assist vs strict quickly.
carla: yes. config surface: {"mode": "strict|assist|off", "sample_rate": "0-1", "staleness_ms": int, "backoff_policy": "auto|manual"}.
ben: one more: telemetry labels for every hint: origin (proxy), staleness_ms, confidence, sample_id. store in request trace.
ria: and create a dashboard that correlates hint-usage with cost/latency/regressions. add alert if hint-influenced error-rate spikes.
dave: interface boundary thought: is proxy part of router codebase (library) or a separate sidecar? pros/cons?
carla: separate sidecar first — easier rollout and per-cluster tuning. long-term we can inline as a library for low-latency tenants.
alice: sidecar simplifies ops but increases network hops. ensure we measure p99 network overhead.
carla: noted. also plan an integration test that replays traces with and without proxy to ensure no functional drift.
ben: ok next steps: 1) formalize hint proto (fields + TTL + provenance), 2) add runtime health topic + backpressure hook, 3) telemetry schema + dash, 4) canary bypass header, 5) per-tenant Console toggle.
omar (pm): timeline? we want an experiment in next sprint.
carla: i'll open RFC follow-up with protos + sample traces today. aim to ship canary toggle + sidecar canary next sprint.
ria: i'll sketch the telemetry dashboard template and necessary metrics.
dave: I'll help add backpressure hooks to the runtime.
ben: I'll review the proto and a short simulation harness to tune sampling.
carla: thanks all — pushing the RFC follow-up now. :rocket:
